This study prioritized focusing on modeling OTEC using existing equipment, making it obvious that research is necessary to develop larger and more efficient OTEC components. Below is a list of remaining uncertainties and potential areas to study further feasibility and knowledge gaps, once again listed in no particular order. • Improved temperature data through local temperature measurements at/near locations considering OTEC is needed to validate year-round temperatures. • A hydrodynamic study of the add-on concept will be crucial for evaluating its feasibility • Since the efficiency and maintenance costs of heat exchangers are key cost drivers of conceptualized OTEC systems, the development of "self-cleaning" heat exchangers will help greatly reduce the cost of OTEC-produced power • This study focused on the coupling of OTEC with new facilities, which was viewed as the first step in establishing the theoretical baseline of the possibility of coupling OTEC with oil and gas facilities.
